name: Orateur
task: Someone — or an AI — to answer the calls we miss
summary: AI phone receptionist for small businesses in Switzerland and French-speaking Europe: answers calls around the clock, books appointments in Google Calendar or Outlook, takes messages and transfers calls.
best_for: small businesses in Switzerland and French-speaking Europe, such as clinics, salons, fiduciaries and law offices, that miss calls and want an AI receptionist to answer, book appointments and take messages around the clock
skip_if: you need callers served in a language other than English or French today, because the pricing FAQ still names only those two and we did not test calls in the other languages the app lists, you need pricing in euros, or you need calendar sync beyond Google Calendar and Outlook
honest_knock: Orateur is built for Swiss and French-speaking businesses (its testimonials are from Lausanne and Geneva). The public pricing page shows Swiss francs in French and pounds in English (read 10 November 2026, pounds again on 17 November). Inside the app, in our own test session on 17 November 2026, the billing page showed the plans in US dollars: Creator $49, Pro $99 and Scale $199 a month, or $490, $990 and $1,990 a year. Orateur also says different things about languages. The pricing FAQ, read again on 17 November 2026, still says the AI supports English and French; the FAQ on its affiliate page says the service is available in English, French, German and Italian; and in our test session the receptionist settings offered a voice and greeting per language for French, English, German, Italian, Hebrew and Arabic, next to a region setting for the United Kingdom, France and the French, German and Italian parts of Switzerland. We only switched languages on in the settings and did not hold a call in any language, so we cannot say how well the AI handles German, Italian, Hebrew or Arabic callers. The pricing FAQ also claims end-to-end encrypted calls and SOC 2 Type II compliance; we have not seen a report. Calendar sync is named for Google Calendar and Outlook only.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-11-03 on orateur.ai/pricing, shown in Swiss francs on the French-language site; on 10 November 2026 the English-language version of the same page showed the same plan figures in pounds, £49, £99 and £199 a month, and no euro or dollar list) Orateur prices by plan, each with an allowance of AI agent time. Creator costs CHF 49 a month with 4 hours of agent time, 1 user, a free phone number, call history and analytics, and email support; extra minutes cost CHF 0.24. Pro costs CHF 99 a month with 9 hours, 2 users and priority support; extra minutes CHF 0.22. Scale costs CHF 199 a month with 19 hours and 5 users; extra minutes CHF 0.20. Enterprise is custom priced through sales. Paying annually gives two months free, according to the pricing toggle; we did not see the annual totals written out. You start with 100 free minutes and no commitment. The page has a cost calculator: at 500 minutes a month it recommends Pro, and shows Creator at CHF 111.40 once the extra minutes are added.

schema_offer.description: Creator, Creator billed monthly: 4 hours of AI agent time a month, 1 user, a free phone number, extra minutes CHF 0.24; Pro CHF 99 (9 hours), Scale CHF 199 (19 hours); annual billing gives 2 months free; 100 free minutes to start. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-03.

claims.claim: Swiss clinics and salons that miss calls
claims.observed: The receptionist was set up with a clinic style instruction and a language, but no real call, calendar link or phone number was used, so nothing was seen about missed calls being answered.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Dossier audience wording versus a receptionist that was only configured, with no call made.
claims.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about whether a clinic stops missing calls.

claims.claim: Busy offices with many calls a month
claims.observed: The plans show minutes and a credit of about 1 second of call time, but SMS costs and a busy month were not tried, so the bill for high call volume could not be checked.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Dossier busy office wording versus plan pages and an account without any calls.
claims.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about how the bill grows for a busy office.

claims.claim: Hallo! Wie kann ich Ihnen heute helfen?
claims.observed: The receptionist has six language tabs (French, English, German, Italian, Hebrew and Arabic); German could be made Active with a German voice and a German first message, and was switched off again. No call was made in it, so how well it speaks German is unknown.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Dossier statement that the app fits English and French callers versus six language tabs in the app; no call was made in any language.
claims.buying_consequence: The app offers more than English and French, but how well the other languages work on a call was not tried.

claims.claim: 1 credit ≈ 1 second of AI call time.
claims.observed: The account showed Available Credits 6.000 with about 1h 40m of call time, which is 100 minutes at one credit per second, as the dossier says about 100 free minutes to start; where the credits came from was not seen.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Dossier 100 free minutes versus the credit balance and the FAQ conversion of one credit to one second.
claims.buying_consequence: The starting balance equals the 100 minutes of the dossier, as long as a credit is one second.

claims.observed: The Monthly tab shows Creator at $ 49,00 /mo in US dollars with about 240 minutes and 1 user; the dossier has CHF 49 for 4 hours of agent time, the same number in another currency.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Dossier price in Swiss francs versus the app price in US dollars, with no exchange rate seen.
claims.buying_consequence: The headline monthly number is the same but in dollars instead of francs, so the amounts are not equal in value.

claims.observed: The plan cards show US$ 0,24, 0,22 and 0,18 per extra minute for Creator, Pro and Scale; the dossier has CHF 0.24, 0.22 and 0.20, so the Scale rate also differs in the number.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Dossier extra minute rates in Swiss francs versus the dollar rates on the cards, with no exchange rate seen.
claims.buying_consequence: The extra minute rates are in another currency and the top plan number differs.

claims.observed: On the Yearly tab Creator is $ 490,00, Pro $ 990,00 and Scale $ 1.990,00 a year, which is ten times the monthly prices of $ 49, $ 99 and $ 199, so two months are free as the dossier says.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Dossier annual wording versus the yearly prices in the app, both read as ten months of the monthly price.
claims.buying_consequence: Paying for a year saves two months of the monthly price.

claims.observed: Get Creator opened Stripe Checkout with Subscribe to Creator $49.00 per month and a Pay and subscribe button, which agrees with the plan card of $ 49,00 /mo; nothing was entered and no total with tax was seen.
claims.plan: Creator monthly, Stripe Checkout, not entered
claims.comparability: Plan page price versus the checkout amount; no stored cost rule was compared.
claims.buying_consequence: The checkout amount equals the plan page price in dollars, and no tax line was seen.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Orateur in a test account: the language and region setting, the set-up of the AI receptionist (agent name, instructions and the six language tabs), the plan page in US dollars on the Monthly and Yearly tabs, the Stripe Checkout for Creator (nothing entered) and the place of the Delete Account button. No real call was made and nothing was paid. Start and account: the test started at about 16:06 (Dutch time) in a test our account on the vendor app, already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English and the region was United Kingdom (Settings, Account, Region, Choose your language and region., with the options United Kingdom, France and the Swiss variants in French, German and Italian). There was no separate French interface to switch. The dashboard showed 0 appointments, 0 calls in the last 7 days and No upcoming appointments. No registration, card, phone number or call was asked. Core action, set up the AI receptionist (Receptionist AI, General): the agent name Manon was changed to Test Receptionist and a test text was typed in Instructions (a clinic name, a warm formal tone, parking, and taking a message when the caller asks about pricing); the page said Saving... and saves by itself. Under Languages & voices there are six tabs: French (Default and Active), English, German, Italian, Hebrew and Arabic. English was off and was switched on; its first message is Hello! How can I help you today? with the voice [GB] Clarice. German can be made Active, with the voice [DE] Berta Berlin and the first message Hallo! Wie kann ich Ihnen heute helfen?, and was switched off again. Our typing tool dropped two letters in the instruction text, which is not an app fault. The setup took about 4 minutes and 8 steps (open the settings, the name, the instructions, a language tab and Active); the times may be unreliable because of our tool. The settings stayed saved. No real call was made: the Test call button, the phone number, the calendar link, SMS, the knowledge base, Services, Staff and Clients were not used, and the tabs Call Settings, Rules, Knowledge Gaps and Tools were not opened. Plans: Settings, Billing shows Available Credits 6.000 (about 1h 40m of call time) and the button Add 15 min for $ 3,60. Monthly: Creator $ 49,00 /mo with about 240 minutes, US$ 0,24/min for additional credits and 1 user; Pro $ 99,00 /mo with about 540 minutes, US$ 0,22/min and 2 users; Scale $ 199,00 /mo with about 1,140 minutes, US$ 0,18/min and 5 users; Enterprise Custom; each plan has a free phone number included. Yearly (2 months free): Creator $ 490,00 /yr, Pro $ 990,00 /yr and Scale $ 1.990,00 /yr. The FAQ says 1 credit is about 1 second of AI call time, that phone numbers are temporarily disabled until you add credits or upgrade, and that you can cancel anytime, that unused credits stay on the account and that the phone number stays reserved for 30 days after a subscription ends. The prices are in US dollars, where the dossier has Swiss francs. Checkout: Get Creator opened Stripe Checkout of the vendor company with Subscribe to Creator $49.00 per month, the button Pay and subscribe and the payment choices Apple Pay, Link, Amazon Pay and card. Nothing was entered and we went back. The screenshot of it was thrown away because the page showed an e-mail address that could not be hidden. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Settings, Account has a section Delete Account with a red Delete button; our tool refused the click and it was not tried again, so no account was deleted. A cancellation of a subscription was not seen; the FAQ says cancelling is possible anytime. Not tested: Test call with the browser microphone, a phone number, linking Google or Microsoft, the calendar, SMS (30 credits per message according to the dossier), the knowledge base, Services, Staff and Clients. Clean up: the account stays; the test data is the agent name Test Receptionist, the instruction text and English switched on (German was switched off again). No subscription and no payment. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app offers six languages where the dossier says English and French only, the prices are in US dollars where the dossier has Swiss francs, a credit is one second of call time so the plan minutes need a conversion, our typing tool dropped two letters in the instruction text, the Delete click was refused by our tool, and the checkout screenshot could not be kept because it showed an e-mail address.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Orateur in a test account: the language and region setting, the set-up of the AI receptionist (agent name, instructions and the six language tabs), the plan page in US dollars on the Monthly and Yearly tabs, the Stripe Checkout for Creator (nothing entered) and the place of the Delete Account button. No real call was made and nothing was paid. Start and account: the test started at about 16:06 (Dutch time) in a test our account on the vendor app, already logged in, in our own tab. The app was already in English and the region was United Kingdom (Settings, Account, Region, Choose your language and region., with the options United Kingdom, France and the Swiss variants in French, German and Italian). There was no separate French interface to switch. The dashboard showed 0 appointments, 0 calls in the last 7 days and No upcoming appointments. No registration, card, phone number or call was asked. Core action, set up the AI receptionist (Receptionist AI, General): the agent name Manon was changed to Test Receptionist and a test text was typed in Instructions (a clinic name, a warm formal tone, parking, and taking a message when the caller asks about pricing); the page said Saving... and saves by itself. Under Languages & voices there are six tabs: French (Default and Active), English, German, Italian, Hebrew and Arabic. English was off and was switched on; its first message is Hello! How can I help you today? with the voice [GB] Clarice. German can be made Active, with the voice [DE] Berta Berlin and the first message Hallo! Wie kann ich Ihnen heute helfen?, and was switched off again. Our typing tool dropped two letters in the instruction text, which is not an app fault. The setup took about 4 minutes and 8 steps (open the settings, the name, the instructions, a language tab and Active); the times may be unreliable because of our tool. The settings stayed saved. No real call was made: the Test call button, the phone number, the calendar link, SMS, the knowledge base, Services, Staff and Clients were not used, and the tabs Call Settings, Rules, Knowledge Gaps and Tools were not opened. Plans: Settings, Billing shows Available Credits 6.000 (about 1h 40m of call time) and the button Add 15 min for $ 3,60. Monthly: Creator $ 49,00 /mo with about 240 minutes, US$ 0,24/min for additional credits and 1 user; Pro $ 99,00 /mo with about 540 minutes, US$ 0,22/min and 2 users; Scale $ 199,00 /mo with about 1,140 minutes, US$ 0,18/min and 5 users; Enterprise Custom; each plan has a free phone number included. Yearly (2 months free): Creator $ 490,00 /yr, Pro $ 990,00 /yr and Scale $ 1.990,00 /yr. The FAQ says 1 credit is about 1 second of AI call time, that phone numbers are temporarily disabled until you add credits or upgrade, and that you can cancel anytime, that unused credits stay on the account and that the phone number stays reserved for 30 days after a subscription ends. The prices are in US dollars, where the dossier has Swiss francs. Checkout: Get Creator opened Stripe Checkout of the vendor company with Subscribe to Creator $49.00 per month, the button Pay and subscribe and the payment choices Apple Pay, Link, Amazon Pay and card. Nothing was entered and we went back. The screenshot of it was thrown away because the page showed an e-mail address that could not be hidden. Cancelling: no subscription ran. Settings, Account has a section Delete Account with a red Delete button; our tool refused the click and it was not tried again, so no account was deleted. A cancellation of a subscription was not seen; the FAQ says cancelling is possible anytime. Not tested: Test call with the browser microphone, a phone number, linking Google or Microsoft, the calendar, SMS (30 credits per message according to the dossier), the knowledge base, Services, Staff and Clients. Clean up: the account stays; the test data is the agent name Test Receptionist, the instruction text and English switched on (German was switched off again). No subscription and no payment. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The app offers six languages where the dossier says English and French only, the prices are in US dollars where the dossier has Swiss francs, a credit is one second of call time so the plan minutes need a conversion, our typing tool dropped two letters in the instruction text, the Delete click was refused by our tool, and the checkout screenshot could not be kept because it showed an e-mail address.
